newsitem.title: USA: Calif. seen voting on unbundling electric services.
newsitem.headline: Calif. seen voting on unbundling electric services.

text.p: California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) is likely to vote Tuesday on whether to allow competition for electricity services such as metering and billing.
A proposed decision issued by a CPUC administrative law judge earlier this year called for "unbundling" of such distribution cost as the industry deregulates.
The agenda for the commission's Tuesday meeting in San Francisco includes a final vote on the proposal.
Under state legislation passed last year, California will begin to phase-out regulated monopoly electric utilities from January of next year.
Through devices such as a centralized "power exchange," power suppliers will be able to compete on the basis of price for customers within the state.
But the issue of whether to open competition for services such as metering and billing has been hotly debated, with consumer groups arguing that customers should have more choices.
The state's largest utilities are opposed to unbundling of costs such as metering and billing and would prefer to retain their existing distribution service monopolies.
The ALJ opinion, however, concluded that "competing energy providers should be allowed to present consolidated bills that reflect the full cost of electricity" and to provide their own meters.
"This could be an opportunity for other companies to compete with utilities in areas other than electricity supplies," a CPUC spokeswoman said.
